description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three LLaMA-2 model variants — LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B — on the CoLeG-R benchmark (%), under four different fine-tuning conditions: no SFT (supervised fine-tuning), + SFT on D₀, + SFT on D₀,D₁, and + SFT on D₀,D₁,D₂. The vertical axis represents CoLeG-R score in percentage, ranging from 0 to 80 with tick marks every 10 units. The horizontal axis lists the three model sizes. For each model, four bars are grouped together, each with a distinct fill pattern and color corresponding to the legend: solid gray-blue for “no SFT”, horizontal-striped tan for “+ SFT on D₀”, diagonal-striped lavender for “+ SFT on D₀,D₁”, and solid maroon for “+ SFT on D₀,D₁,D₂”. Performance generally increases with both model size and the number of datasets used in SFT. For example, LLaMA-2-7B scores approximately 67% with no SFT and rises to ~83% with SFT on all three datasets. Similarly, LLaMA-2-13B improves from ~70% to ~80%, and LLaMA-2-70B from ~80% to ~83%. The chart visually supports the paper’s investigation into whether larger LLMs benefit more from incremental supervised fine-tuning on increasingly complex datasets when solving longer math word problems.
